title: Binary search that halves the range and never overflows

blocks.text: Binary search is the page's O(log n) example: compare the target with the middle element and **keep only the half that can still hold it**, so a million elements take about 20 probes. Two edge cases from the page: a range of **one element must still be checked**, and `(left + right) / 2` **overflows** on huge ranges, so the middle is `left + (right - left) / 2`.

Write `BinarySearch.indexOf(values, target)`. `values` is a sorted `BinarySearch.SortedInts` (given): `size()` and `get(i)`. Return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is absent. The tests count every `get` call.

cases.says: In [1, 3, 5, 7, 9], 7 is at index 3, 1 at index 0, and 4 is absent (-1).
Searching a sorted sequence of 1,000,000 values reads at most 20 elements, whatever the target.
In a sequence of Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1 elements, a target near the end is found, so the middle index never overflows.
A single-element sequence finds its element, and the last element of [1, 3, 5, 7, 9] is found.

concepts: An O(log n) algorithm such as binary search halves the remaining range with each step, so a million elements take about 20 probes.
The middle index is left + (right - left) / 2, because (left + right) / 2 overflows on large ranges.
